title: Pico Startup Sequence
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Clocks and Watches with AI
description: A clickable flowchart of what the Pico does from power-on to a running clock, with a toggle that shows how the path changes when main.py is missing.

learningObjectives: Describe the steps from power-on to a running clock program
Explain the roles of boot.py and main.py
Explain what changes when there is no main.py, and how Thonny can interrupt a running main.py
prerequisites: Saving files to the Pico with Thonny

accessibility.notes: Controls are standard HTML form elements

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Annotated process diagram with a compare-the-cases toggle
keyQuestions: Which file runs first, boot.py or main.py?
What does the Pico do at power-up if there is no main.py?
Why can Thonny stop main.py but a battery-powered clock cannot be stopped?
commonMisconceptions: The Pico runs whichever file was opened last in Thonny
boot.py is where the clock program belongs
Unplugging from the computer deletes main.py
assessmentOpportunities: Students put the startup steps in order without the diagram.
Students explain why a program named clock.py does not start at power-up.
Students describe two ways to interrupt a running main.py.

controls.label: Step
controls.description: Shows an explanation of that step
